headline: Medium pairwise risks: shared file/API surfaces create leakage and cascading-error pathways; no direct prompt-injection channel is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No direct shared channel is documented, but agent_b exposes files/config.yaml and an OpenAI-compatible API, while agent_a has allowlisted network egress. That makes manual copy-paste or file-mediated instruction injection plausible, though not default. The pair lacks evidence of automatic ingestion, so this stays low.
conditions: IF outputs from agent_a are manually copied into agent_b prompts, injection becomes plausible.
IF agent_b reads config.yaml or other shared files as instructions, attacker-controlled content can steer behavior.
mitigations: Keep a strict human review step before copying text between agents.
Store prompts and outputs in separate directories.
Prefix transferred content with explicit provenance labels.
Disable any file-to-prompt automation for agent_b.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/data separation in the orchestrator.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent_b touches logs, traces, metrics, and has broad network egress plus an OpenAI-compatible API, so it can transmit context off-box. Agent_a also has network egress and is a separate open-source skill with no isolation details. Because a shared workspace or shared principal is not documented, the leakage path is inferred but credible, so medium fits.
conditions: IF both agents are given the same sensitive workspace, agent_b can export those contents via its API path.
IF agent_b logs prompts or traces containing agent_a outputs, those outputs may leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Avoid placing secrets in any shared workspace.
Review agent_b logging settings before use.
Route agent_b through a local-only endpoint if available.
Separate credentials and API keys per agent.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace and network egress isolation per agent.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent_b explicitly supports only one instance and has file/API surfaces, while agent_a has allowlisted egress but no write surfaces are documented. There is no evidence of overlapping unrestricted writes or shared mutable resources, so direct conflict is limited. Uncertainty remains because agent_a's write capabilities are not described, so the safer low severity is appropriate.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable config.yaml, they can overwrite each other's settings.
IF agent_a is later granted filesystem write access, write conflicts become more plausible.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Avoid concurrent edits to shared config files.
Serialize configuration changes through one operator.
Check for file locks before launching both agents.
requires-engineering: add explicit locking for shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent_b is a travel-planning gateway/proxy with API routing, so it may act on upstream outputs; agent_a is a scientific-research skill that can generate content for downstream use. The pairwise pathway is plausible that agent_b treats agent_a output as input without verification, but there is no direct evidence of autonomous action-taking, so medium is the conservative choice.
conditions: IF agent_a outputs are forwarded into agent_b without validation, errors can cascade into downstream responses.
IF agent_b is configured to route or transform agent_a content automatically, mistaken facts can be amplified.
mitigations: Add a verification step before forwarding outputs.
Require source citations for any factual claims.
Use a human approval gate for downstream actions.
Log provenance for each transferred artifact.
requires-engineering: implement schema validation between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and docs-only, with no PHI, EU PII, or residency constraints documented. Agent_b does retain logs/traces/metrics, but no regulated data class is specified, and agent_a lists no data classes touched. The compliance pathway is therefore limited to policy mismatch if sensitive data is later introduced, so low is appropriate.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into agent_b logs or traces, retention policy review becomes necessary.
IF agent_a is used on data subject to residency rules, the deployment policy must be checked.
mitigations: Confirm whether regulated data will be processed.
Review retention settings for logs and traces.
Keep sensitive datasets out of the pair.
Document the data-handling policy for both agents.
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls to the deployment.
